*Generated by `src/build_report.py` from pipeline outputs. Raw files in `data/raw/` are never modified.*

Provenance: facility KMLs, the hospitals CSV and the ward polygons come from OpenCity (data.opencity.in), which
lists MCGM as the original source. The facility dataset metadata was last modified 2025-11-27; its resources were
created 2025-11-25. The census files are from the OpenCity "Mumbai – Ward wise Census Data" dataset (Census of
India 2011). Downloaded 2026-10-19. The PRD expected a supplied 2023 ward population file. None was available, so
**Census 2011 population is used and labelled `population_2011` throughout**.

## 2. Facility records

| Layer | Raw records | Kept | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dispensary | 186 | 186 | |
| UPHC | 211 | 211 | |
| Public hospital | 31 | 31 | |
| Maternity home | 28 | 28 | |

* Records excluded: **0** (no exact duplicates; no within-layer probable duplicates; every ward value
  standardized). Exclusion log: `outputs/tables/exclusion_log.csv`.
* Same-name facilities in *different* wards (e.g. Kajupada in L and R/C; Shastri Nagar in H/W and R/N) are
  distinct records with different coordinates and are **not** merged.
* Missing values: one maternity home (Deonar, M/E) has no coordinates. It is kept in the ward counts (its source
  ward is known) and left off maps. One dispensary has an empty address.

## 3. Ward standardization

Source layers mix two spellings of the same ward (e.g. `KE` and `K/E`). Mapping is structural only (insert the
slash between ward letter and direction suffix) and every result is checked against the 24 polygon names.
Full mapping with record counts: `outputs/tables/ward_value_mapping.csv`. Unmapped values: none.

## 4. Co-location (distinct physical sites)

A pair of records is treated as one physical site only when **all three** hold: same standardized ward; identical
name stem after removing facility-type words ("Dispensary", "UPHC", "Maternity Home", …); and coordinates within
300 m plus the worst-case rounding error of each point. Name similarity or proximity alone never merges records.

* Candidate pairs: 58; matched: **54**;
  rejected as too far apart: 3; undecidable (missing coordinates):
  1.
* Matches by layer pair: Dispensary + Maternity home: 4; Dispensary + UPHC: 48; UPHC + Maternity home: 2.
* Result: 456 facility records → **402 distinct sites**, of which
  54 offer more than one category. Category counts therefore sum to more than the site total.
* 4 matches rely on
  the tolerance (distance > 0); the largest is 1530 m. All pairs
  and decisions: `outputs/tables/colocation_candidate_pairs.csv`.

## 5. Coordinates

* Status: {'valid': 455, 'missing': 1}.
* Precision (decimal places): {'1': 5, '2': 393, '4': 57, '<NA>': 1}. Most points are rounded to 2 decimals (≈ 1.1 km lat,
  ≈ 1.05 km lon), so locations are approximate.
* All valid points fall inside a generous Greater Mumbai bounding box.

## 6. Ward assignment

Priority 1 is the facility's own `Ward` attribute. Each point was also spatially joined to the ward polygons
(EPSG:4326, distances in EPSG:32643) as a check:

| check | records |
|---|---|
| agree | 387 |
| disagree_within_coordinate_rounding | 43 |
| disagree_review | 20 |
| outside_polygons_review | 4 |
| outside_polygons_within_rounding | 1 |
| no_valid_coordinates | 1 |

"Within rounding" means the point lies outside its source ward by no more than its coordinate-rounding error.
24 records need review (listed in `outputs/tables/ward_assignment_review.csv`). Several are pairs of
co-located records sharing one bad coordinate. One (New Centenary dispensary/UPHC, source ward R/S) plots
≈ 15 km away in M/W, which points to a coordinate error rather than a ward error. The source ward is kept for all
records; no ward was reassigned from coordinates.

## 7. Ward polygons

24 polygons, names identical to the 24-ward list, all geometrically valid (repaired: 0).
Total area 474.4 km². The polygon file has no publication date. The BMC ward structure can change, so
the delimitation date is unverified.

## 8. Population (Census 2011)

| check | passed |
|---|---|
| all census ward names map to a BMC ward | True |
| census ward codes unique | True |
| ward-code prefix agrees with ward name for every row | True |
| every census ward found in Primary Census Abstract | True |
| ward populations equal PCA TOT_P | True |
| total equals sum of the two district TOWN totals (Greater Mumbai) | True |
| 24 wards with positive population | True |

97 census wards aggregate to the 24 BMC wards; total **12,442,373**.

## 9. Hospitals list CSV (reconciliation only)

The ward-wise hospitals CSV (288 rows; types {'Private': 235, 'Municipal': 33, 'Government': 13, 'Govt': 3, 'Trust': 2, 'BMC': 1, 'Defence': 1})
has no coordinates or ids and is mostly private, so it is **not** added to the counts. Its 51
public rows (Municipal/BMC/Government/Govt/Defence; Trust and Private excluded) were matched to the KML hospital and
maternity layers by name within ward, plus 9 documented manual decisions
(`data/reference/hospital_list_manual_matches.csv`). Results: {'matched_in_kml': 32, 'not_found_in_kml_layers': 18, 'matched_in_kml_ward_conflict': 1}.
No CSV rows list ward C.
